name: Zip2 Corporation

summary.text: Zip2 Corporation was an online city-guide and mapping software company. Compaq Computer Corporation announced on February 16, 1999 that it had agreed to buy all of Zip2's shares for cash, completed the purchase in April 1999 for about $307 million in cash (about $341 million including employee stock options and costs), and folded it into its AltaVista search business. Tesla's 2010 registration statement lists Zip2 among Elon Musk's earlier roles; secondary accounts describe it as the first company he co-founded.

facts.claim: A Compaq release dated February 16, 1999, filed with the SEC, said Compaq had reached a definitive agreement to acquire Zip2 Corp. in a cash purchase of all outstanding shares, and that Zip2's board had unanimously approved the deal.
facts.quote: A Compaq release dated February 16, 1999 said it had reached a definitive agreement to acquire Zip2 Corp. The deal was a cash purchase of all outstanding shares, and Zip2's board had unanimously approved it.

facts.claim: Compaq completed the Zip2 acquisition in early April 1999 by cash tender offer; a Compaq release dated April 5, 1999 announced the completion. AltaVista's 1999 S-1 gives an aggregate purchase price of $340.9 million, consisting of $307.2 million in cash, employee stock options with a fair value of $27.7 million and other acquisition costs; Compaq's 1999 annual report gives about $341 million including $307 million in cash and options valued at $28 million. Zip2 became a unit of AltaVista, the search engine Compaq had recently acquired.

openQuestions: Musk's proceeds from the Zip2 sale (about $22 million, with about $15 million to Kimbal Musk) appear only in secondary accounts citing Ashlee Vance's biography; one X post gives $21 million. No filing, and no contemporaneous NYT, CNET or LA Times coverage, was retrieved this session (the search budget ran out before a major-outlet search could run).
Zip2's founding date, founders and investors (Mohr Davidow Ventures' 1996 investment) are already recorded in research/findings/elon-musk.json from the Washington Post; they were not re-sourced here.

The brief's premise that Zip2 or X.com was capitalised with money from Errol Musk's Zambian emerald dealings: the only sources are the Musk family's own, conflicting statements ($28,000 per Vance's biography; 10% of a roughly $200,000 angel round 'much later' per Elon Musk's 2019 tweet), already recorded in elon-musk.json. No source retrieved this session connects emerald proceeds to Zip2's or X.com's funding, or mentions South African exchange controls.
The AltaVista S-1 gives the Zip2 closing as effective April 1, 1999 in one place and April 2, 1999 in another, per the search summary; the exact closing date should be checked in the filing.
